content: Palisades Medical Center is a regional hospital located in North Bergen, New Jersey. The facility has a capacity of approximately 202 beds and provides medical services to an estimated population of 350,000 individuals residing in Southern Bergen and Hudson counties. Since 1999, the hospital has been a member of the NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital network and maintains an academic affiliation with the Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons. Historically, the hospital was previously known as North Hudson Hospital, which was situated in Weehawken, New Jersey. In 1978, the hospital was relocated to the North Bergen waterfront and subsequently renamed Palisades Medical Center. On September 21, 2007, actor George Clooney and a companion were admitted to Palisades Medical Center for treatment following a motorcycle accident. Information regarding Clooney's status as a patient at the hospital was leaked to the media prior to any official statement from the hospital. This prompted hospital officials to suspect an internal breach of confidentiality. An internal audit revealed that 27 employees had accessed Clooney's medical records without proper authorization. As a result, all 27 employees were suspended for one month without pay. The individuals involved included nurses, support staff, and security personnel, but no physicians were implicated. A union representing some of the staff members has contested seven of the suspensions.
